Two of the three fixes are correct: the check that rejects weights over 20.0 kg matches the docstring, and `int(total + 0.5)` gives the documented round-half-up behaviour. An integer-only version would be sturdier: `(base*(100+pct)+50)//100`.

Blocking: switching `<=` to `<` in the tier loop contradicts the docstring. It says each tier limit "is inclusive: a parcel weighing exactly a tier's limit belongs to that tier, not the next one." The change was made only to satisfy `test_two_kilo_parcel_zone1`, which expects 2.0 kg to cost 1290 and so contradicts the docstring. It silently changes pricing at every boundary (for example, 0.5 kg now costs 790 instead of 450, and 5.0 kg costs 2450 instead of 1290). The docstring still says "inclusive", so the code now contradicts its own documentation. The PR also claims the change matches the carrier spec without mentioning that the documented spec says the opposite.

This is customer-facing pricing, so please ask the teammate or the carrier partnerships team which rule is right. If boundaries are inclusive, the test is wrong and needs updating with their sign-off. If they're exclusive, keep `<` and update the docstring and its tier table to match. Either way, the PR description should state the conflict plainly.
